b:
This
is not common property;
it is a privately owned poem

Even after
a quarter of a century
he lives in my memories
mostly
as quarter-hour
voices on the telephone

At the age to hold me
on his chest and pamper me
he stood alone
in the Middle Eastern sun

Even today
he stands
alone …..

My college
life
was for him
only
stories passed on by word of mouth;
he never saw
a single picture of it

Even when I had grown
as tall as his shoulder,
the fatherhood of the older generation
never
showed friendship,

the certificates of praise
he never let fall
in front of me
in daylight

To eavesdrop late at night
as he whispers them
in Amma's ear
is a joy of its own

For the man
who took
my future
as his only
desire,
if not like a flood of rain,
then like the light of a sparkler,

for the man
who does not want
change
in tradition:
a gift
of free verse
note: "Free verse" is puthukkavithai, literally "new poetry", which breaks with the traditional metres, a gentle joke for a father who dislikes change. "Common property" (pothuvudamai) is also the Tamil word for communism.
